name: Perfect-fluid continuity / first law in FLRW: d(rho a^3) = -p d(a^3), dS = 0; rho a^{3(1+w)} = const

source.located: Textbook result with no single primary arXiv source. Continuity half READ in Baumann, 'TASI Lectures on Inflation', arXiv:0907.5424v2, p.20 eqs (21)-(26) and Problem eqs (112)-(113). The dS = 0 half READ as an explicitly stated ASSUMPTION in Bousso, 'The holographic principle', arXiv:hep-th/0203101v2 Sect. 7.1 eqs (7.4)-(7.5) ('We will assume, for now, that the universe evolves adiabatically ... The comoving entropy density s is constant in space and time'), and in Masoumi & Mathur arXiv:1412.2618v2 Fig. 4 caption ('assume that entropy is conserved in each comoving volume') with first law eq (24) 'T dS = dE + p dV' (no mu dN term). Classics NAMED-NOT-READ: Weinberg 1971 ApJ 168, 175 (bulk-viscous entropy production); Kolb & Turner 1990 'The Early Universe' ch.3 (s a^3 conserved in thermal equilibrium); Weinberg 1972 'Gravitation and Cosmology'.

published_statement: Baumann 0907.5424 p.20: 'Eqns. (21) and (22) may be combined into the continuity equation d rho/dt + 3H(rho + p) = 0 (23). This may also be written as d ln rho / d ln a = -3(1+w) (24), if we define the equation of state parameter w = p/rho (25). Eqn. (24) may be integrated to give rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)} (26).' Problem (113): 'Derive the continuity equation from nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0.' Bousso hep-th/0203101 Sect. 7.1: 'We will assume, for now, that the universe evolves adiabatically. Thus, the physical entropy density is diluted by cosmological expansion: sigma(eta) = s / a(eta)^3 (7.5). The comoving entropy density s is constant in space and time.'
published_hypotheses: Homogeneous, isotropic FLRW metric (any k); Baumann eq (20) perfect-fluid T_mu_nu = diag(rho, -p, -p, -p) in the comoving frame
Perfect fluid: no shear or bulk viscosity, no heat flux (T_mu_nu of form (20))
Either the Einstein equations (Friedmann eqs 21-22) or, independently, local conservation nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0 (Problem 113) -- either suffices for continuity
For the closed form rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)}: w = p/rho constant (Baumann integrates (24) with w fixed)

For dS = 0: adiabatic evolution is ASSUMED (Bousso 7.1 'We will assume, for now'); the thermodynamic route requires a Gibbs relation T dS = dE + p dV - mu dN in local equilibrium with mu dN = 0 (Masoumi-Mathur eq (24) writes T dS = dE + p dV, i.e. fixed N)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (thermodynamic step): permute.py:256 docstring 'd(rho a^3) + p d(a^3), which is T dS' identifies the continuity residual with T dS without naming the Gibbs relation, local thermodynamic equilibrium, or mu dN = 0; re-derivation check (4c) shows continuity alone leaves T dS = -mu dN.

DROPPED (perfect-fluid qualifier in the conclusion): permute.py:80-81 carries 'for a comoving volume of perfect fluid', but permute.py:85 'THE EXPANSION IS ISENTROPIC', permute.py:274 'EXPANSION_DISSIPATES = False', the scorecard permute.py:508 'the expansion is isentropic' and verdict permute.py:541-543 'The FLRW expansion is isentropic ... no dissipation' state it of the expansion of the universe unconditionally. With bulk viscosity zeta > 0 (Weinberg 1971, NAMED-NOT-READ) the expansion itself produces entropy T dS/dt = 9 zeta H^2 a^3 (check (5)); with out-of-equilibrium energy exchange between perfect fluids (decays), T dS_r/dt = Gamma rho_m a^3 > 0 (check (6b)).

WEAKENED (assumption presented as measurement): the literature READ treats comoving-entropy conservation as an assumption (Bousso hep-th/0203101 Sect. 7.1; Masoumi-Mathur 1412.2618 Fig. 4); permute.py:84 says it 'is measured below to machine precision'. The tree's check (permute.py:250-270) evaluates rho_of_a -- which IS the continuity solution (permute.py:251) -- against continuity by central difference; it passes any w used consistently (check (8c), w = 5.7) and returns O(1) (0.769) only when rho and p are mismatched (check (8b)). It verifies an identity; it measures no physical system.

DISCREPANCY (precision wording, not a refutation): 'machine precision' (permute.py:84) -- measured relative residuals are 7.3e-12 (radiation), 4.8e-11 (dust), 0 (vacuum), 1.5e-11 (w=-2/3), i.e. finite-difference truncation/roundoff at h = 1e-6, five orders above double epsilon 2.2e-16; the tol 1e-9 (permute.py:268) is what the check actually asserts.

DISCREPANCY (tree-side label, not in the source): permute.py:436 and 449 (and prose at 117) label w = -2/3 'curvature-like'. rho ∝ a^{-3(1+w)} gives a^{-1} for w = -2/3 (domain-wall-like); the curvature term k/a^2 read as a fluid has w = -1/3 (checks (7), (7b)). The first-law check passes for w = -2/3 regardless, so the label does not move this result.
KEPT: constant w (tree hypothesis 1) matches Baumann's integration of (24); the tree does not apply rho a^{3(1+w)} = const to a varying-w component.

rederivation.outcome: ALL 19 CHECKS PASS (exit 0). (1) nabla_mu T^{mu 0} computed from Christoffels of the FLRW metric for general k equals rho' + 3H(rho+p); spatial components vanish. (2) d(rho a^3) + p d(a^3) = a^3 x continuity; (2b) Friedmann (21)+(22) imply continuity for every k. (3) rho0 a^{-3(1+w)} satisfies d(rho a^3) + w rho d(a^3) = 0 exactly for all real w; dsolve returns C a^{-3(1+w)}. (3c) CPL w(a) still solves continuity but rho a^{3(1+w0)} is not constant. (4) radiation T = T0/a solves continuity and gives s a^3 = const; (4c) continuity leaves T dS = -mu dN. (5) bulk viscosity: T dS/dt = 9 zeta H^2 a^3 > 0. (6) dust decaying to radiation: total continuity holds, T dS_r/dt = Gamma rho_m a^3 > 0. (7) w = -1/3 <-> a^-2 (curvature), w = -2/3 <-> a^-1. (8) permute.py imported read-only: fixtures pass, relative residuals 7.3e-12 / 4.8e-11 / 0 / 1.5e-11; mismatched rho,p gives 0.769; an arbitrary consistent w = 5.7 also passes (tautology).

lacked_data: The result is a theorem of local conservation (or of the Friedmann equations via the contracted Bianchi identity) and takes no numerical input, so no later datum can falsify it; re-derived here symbolically for every k. The only data that bear on its USE are (a) which equation of state real components have and (b) whether real components are perfect fluids in equilibrium. (a) DESI DR2 (2503.14738) now prefers an evolving w at 2.8-4.2 sigma: this removes constant w for dark energy, which removes the closed form rho a^{3(1+w)} = const for that component but leaves continuity and perfect-fluid isentropy intact (check 3c) -- no change to the conclusion. (b) Entropy production in the real universe comes from departures from the perfect-fluid/equilibrium hypotheses (bulk viscosity in mixtures, out-of-equilibrium decays, first-order transitions, reheating), a fact available to the classic authors (Weinberg 1971) and not a data gap; it narrows the scope of 'THE EXPANSION IS ISENTROPIC' rather than overturning it. Evidence for M's hypothesis for THIS result: none found; evidence against: the result has no datum to lack.
grade_evidence: The external result itself STANDS: continuity rho' + 3H(rho+p) = 0 <=> d(rho a^3) = -p d(a^3) re-derived from nabla_mu T^{mu nu} = 0 on FLRW for every k and from the Friedmann equations; rho a^{3(1+w)} = const exact for constant w (sympy, 19/19 pass). It is NARROWED as the tree uses it because two hypotheses are dropped: (i) dS = 0 follows only with a Gibbs relation in local equilibrium and mu dN = 0 -- permute.py:256 calls the residual 'T dS' without naming them, and the READ literature (Bousso hep-th/0203101 Sect. 7.1) states comoving adiabaticity as an assumption; (ii) the perfect-fluid qualifier of permute.py:80-81 is dropped in 'THE EXPANSION IS ISENTROPIC' (permute.py:85), EXPANSION_DISSIPATES = False (permute.py:274), the scorecard (permute.py:508) and the verdict (permute.py:541-543) -- a bulk-viscous fluid gives T dS/dt = 9 zeta H^2 a^3 > 0 (check 5), so the expansion can dissipate outside the hypothesis. Not WRONG: within the perfect-fluid/equilibrium hypotheses the claim is exact. Recorded, not repaired: the 'measured to machine precision' wording (actual relative residuals up to 4.8e-11; the check is a tautology of the solution against its own equation, passing any consistent w) and the 'curvature-like' label for w = -2/3 (curvature is w = -1/3) are discrepancies, not refutations, and neither moves the result. No datum moves the conclusion (DESI DR2 evolving w affects only the constant-w closed form).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the hypotheses at the use sites -- scoping 'THE EXPANSION IS ISENTROPIC' / EXPANSION_DISSIPATES = False to a perfect fluid in local equilibrium with mu dN = 0 (the dS = 0 step), as permute.py:80-81 already does for the first-law line. To OPEN on the dS = 0 half: if the Weinberg 1971 / Maartens astro-ph/9609119 bulk-viscosity statements, here NAMED-NOT-READ and reproduced only in form, were read at source and found to differ from the form used in check (5). Nothing identified here would make it WRONG.
